title: Bind qa_approve to the exact candidate the reviewer read
description:
Objective: make an approval apply to the bytes the reviewer actually read. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.ts today checks status and a summary, so an approval issued against one candidate silently blesses whatever the task holds by the time it lands.

Deliverable: qa_approve accepts the reviewed candidate id and rejects the call when that candidate is not the task's current one, with a named error telling the reviewer to re-read. get_context surfaces the current candidate id to QA so the reviewer has it. A Review record is persisted carrying reviewer, decision, the exact reviewed candidate and the summary, and qa_reject records the same binding.

Not in scope: the delivery-evidence gate on DONE, which is the sibling task, and any IDE change. Keep qa_approve's existing soft commit-evidence warnings working; this task adds a hard binding on candidate identity only.

Unskips the acceptance case "reviewing candidate A cannot approve B".

Verification: npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: qa_approve accepts a reviewed candidate id and rejects a mismatch against the task's current candidate with a named error, asserted exactly
qa_reject records the same candidate binding as qa_approve
A Review record persisting reviewer, decision, reviewed candidate and summary is written for both outcomes
get_context returns the current candidate id for a task in REVIEW
A project with no candidate recorded keeps the current approve behaviour, so adoption is incremental
The acceptance case for reviewing candidate A cannot approve B is unskipped and passes unchanged
npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: Keep the existing qa_approve warnings array and commitEvidence; this task adds a hard candidate binding, it does not restructure the tool's result.
A task with no candidate recorded must keep working, so the change is additive.

This task's shape is dictated, not chosen: packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts was authored before any implementation so no later task could redefine delivery, and its rules say a diff that edits an assertion, constant, fixture or helper in that file instead of the code under test is a QA reject. You may change exactly one character in it - the skip on your own case. (a) Read its header, lines 1-70, and transcribe the four normative items that belong to this task into the step note verbatim: moe.qa_approve also accepts candidateId; moe.get_context projects result.currentCandidate as the exact stored Candidate record selected by createdAt then id; the persisted Review carries taskId, candidateId, reviewerId, decision and summary; CANDIDATE_MISMATCH maps to MoeErrorCode -32002. Note also that every new record lives at .moe/<kind>/<id>.json following the resourceStore pattern, so reviews go in .moe/reviews. (b) Read criterion 3 in full, lines 1435-1625, and write down what it asserts BEYOND this card's Definition of Done, because those assertions are binding too: the refusal's context must carry expectedCandidateId and currentCandidateId with exactly those key names; currentCandidate must deep-equal the whole stored candidate file, not just an id; on refusal the task file bytes, BOTH candidate files and an EMPTY reviews directory must all hold; and the positive control expects exactly one review record after approving the current candidate. (c) Read src/tools/qaApprove.ts (179 lines) whole - its result literal at line 155 carries warnings, commitEvidence and message, and a task rail forbids restructuring it. Read src/tools/qaReject.ts and the tail of src/tools/getContext.ts, whose single large return literal begins at line 271. (d) Read src/state/candidateStore.ts and note its exact export list - a test in the candidate task pins it at five exports, so do not add a sixth; listCandidatesForTask already orders by createdAt then id, which is exactly the selection rule, so REUSE it rather than sorting again. (e) Note what NOT to do: ATTEMPT_FINALIZING lives in src/util/claimGuards.ts and gates claiming, not approving, and criterion 3 deliberately finalizes the attempt so that hold is not the refusing layer. Do not fence qa_approve on attempt identity - QA is not the attempt holder, and assertAttemptCurrent here would break the case.

implementationPlan.description: PERSIST THE REVIEW RECORD. In src/types/schema.ts add an exported Review interface carrying id, taskId, candidateId, reviewerId, decision and createdAt, plus the summary, with decision a union of approve and reject. The five field names the acceptance case projects are fixed by the frozen contract; id and createdAt are the record's own, matching every other store. Keep it additive: no existing type changes, no schemaVersion bump, no migration. In src/state/StateManager.ts add a reviews map beside the existing candidates map and one loadEntities call over the reviews directory in load, exactly as the candidates collection was wired. Create src/state/reviewStore.ts as stateless exported functions taking the state handle first, mirroring candidateStore: record, get and a list by task. Reviews are an append-only audit trail, so there is NO update and NO delete function - the function must not exist, which is stronger than a convention not to call one, and a reopened task that is reviewed again simply gets a second record. Persist with writeEntity BEFORE touching the map, so a failed write leaves no review visible. Error handling: validate that taskId, candidateId, reviewerId and summary are non-blank strings and that the decision is one of the two members, refusing with the invalid-input error rather than coercing. Do NOT add a separate reviewStore test file - the named verification command covers src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts and the acceptance file, so the store's cases live in the former.
implementationPlan.note:
Review record persisted. Three files.

schema.ts (+41 lines after the Candidate block, nothing existing changed, no schemaVersion bump,
no migration): `export type ReviewDecision = 'approve' | 'reject'` and `export interface Review`
with id, taskId, candidateId, reviewerId, decision, summary, createdAt — all readonly, matching
Candidate. The five field names the acceptance case projects (taskId, candidateId, reviewerId,
decision, summary) are exactly the frozen contract's; id and createdAt are the record's own, as in
every other store. Docblock states the append-only rule: a re-review APPENDS a second record.

StateManager.ts (3 lines): `Review` added to the existing type-only import list, `reviews` map
beside `candidates` at :386, and one `loadEntities<Review>(.moe/reviews)` in load() right after
the candidates line. loadEntities tolerates a missing directory, so a project that has never
recorded a review loads empty — the incremental-adoption case needs no scaffolding.

state/reviewStore.ts (NEW, 142 lines): stateless exports taking the state handle first, mirroring
candidateStore. Exactly three exports — `recordReview`, `getReview`, `listReviewsForTask`. There
is NO update and NO delete function and no exported validator: the absence is the rail, and
keeping the validator private means one fewer public surface than candidateStore has (its
validate is exported only because record_candidate needs it pre-fence; here both call sites go
through recordReview). Write path is `await state.writeEntity('reviews', id, review)` THEN
`state.reviews.set(...)`, so a failed write leaves no review visible anywhere — that is what lets
step 4 promise an empty reviews directory after a refusal. No appendActivity and no emit, same as
candidateStore/attemptStore: both would need edits to the ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES / StateChangeEvent
unions and there is no consumer yet.

Validation refuses rather than coerces: absent field -> missingRequired, present-but-not-a-string
or blank -> invalidInput, decision outside {approve, reject} -> invalidInput naming both members.
taskId/candidateId/id go through validateEntityId (path-traversal + 128-char bound). reviewerId
deliberately does NOT: the IDE/human approval path records the literal `human`, and a reviewer
seat need not have a persisted worker record when it signs off. Readers hand out copies
(`{ ...review }`), so no caller can mutate stored state through a return value.
listReviewsForTask sorts createdAt-then-id, the same tie-break candidateStore uses.

`npx vitest run src/state/stateModules.test.ts` 3 passed — the structural guards still hold

TDD deviation, stated plainly: the approved plan puts every test for this store in

count). So this step landed production code before its tests. Step 5 owes the red for it by
mutation in a scratch tree per the repo's established recipe, not by a green-only claim.

implementationPlan.description: PROJECT THE CURRENT CANDIDATE FROM get_context. In src/tools/getContext.ts add currentCandidate as a top-level key on the result literal that begins at line 271. Its value is the task's current candidate record - the last one by createdAt then id - obtained through candidateStore's existing list-by-task function so the ordering rule lives in one place and cannot drift from the record_candidate side. Emit the WHOLE stored record, not a projection and not just an id: the acceptance case deep-equals it against the candidate file on disk, so any reshaping or added field fails it. Omit the key entirely when the task has no candidate, rather than emitting null, so a project that has never recorded one sees no change at all. Include it whenever a candidate exists regardless of status, which necessarily covers the REVIEW case the Definition of Done names and also helps a worker about to record a second candidate; a status gate would make the field vanish exactly when a reviewer re-reads a reopened task. Hand out a copy rather than the live cached object, the way the candidate task's own review insisted, so a caller cannot mutate stored state through the response. Change nothing else in that literal - it is the payload every role reads at the start of every task.

implementationPlan.description: BIND BOTH QA DECISIONS TO THE REVIEWED CANDIDATE. In src/tools/qaApprove.ts accept an optional candidateId argument and resolve the task's current candidate through the same list-by-task helper. Decide in this order. If the task has NO candidate at all, behave exactly as today, which is the additive-adoption rail - a project that never records candidates must keep working. If a candidateId is supplied and it does not match the current candidate's id, refuse BEFORE any write with a MoeError carrying the existing state-conflict numeric code, the stable codeName CANDIDATE_MISMATCH, and a context holding exactly expectedCandidateId - what the reviewer read - and currentCandidateId; the message should tell the reviewer to re-read the current candidate, because that is the action. If it matches, proceed. If a candidate exists but candidateId was OMITTED, proceed - adoption is incremental - but push a warning onto the existing warnings array so the gap is visible rather than silent; that array already exists for the commit-evidence warning and a rail forbids restructuring the result, so add to it and change nothing else about warnings, commitEvidence or message. On every successful approval write one Review with decision approve, and write it only after the candidate check has passed, since the acceptance case asserts an EMPTY reviews directory after a refusal. Apply the identical argument, the identical refusal and an identical Review with decision reject in src/tools/qaReject.ts, leaving its existing reopen and failed-item behaviour untouched. Do not add an attempt fence to either tool.
implementationPlan.note:
Both QA decisions are now bound to the reviewed candidate. Three files.

SHARED HELPER, and where it lives. `resolveReviewedCandidate(state, taskId, suppliedId, toolName)`
plus `export const CANDIDATE_MISMATCH` went into the ALREADY-MODIFIED state/reviewStore.ts rather
than a new module. The plan's risk note says "no extra helper" because an eleventh file trips the
hard size limit, and duplicating a named refusal in two tools is exactly what util/claimGuards.ts
exists to prevent. reviewStore is the cohesive home: its whole subject is binding a decision to the
bytes it read, and the helper's output IS the candidateId a Review must carry. It imports
candidateStore (no cycle — candidateStore does not import reviewStore).

DECISION ORDER, implemented exactly as planned:
  1. No candidate recorded -> `{}`. No refusal, no Review, no warning. Byte-identical to the old
     behaviour; this is the additive-adoption rail.
  2. candidateId supplied and != current -> throw MoeError(STATE_CONFLICT = -32002,
     codeName 'CANDIDATE_MISMATCH', context { taskId, expectedCandidateId, currentCandidateId,
     tool }). The two context key names are exactly the ones criterion 3 asserts. Message names
     both ids and tells the reviewer the action: re-read get_context.currentCandidate and decide
     again.
  3. Candidate exists, candidateId omitted -> proceed, bound to the current candidate, plus a
     NO-REVIEWED-CANDIDATE warning. Adoption stays incremental; the gap is visible, not silent.
  4. Match -> proceed, bound.
A candidateId belonging to a DIFFERENT task lands in case 2 automatically: it is compared against
THIS task's current candidate, which it cannot equal. No extra code, no second lookup.
A present-but-blank candidateId is refused (INVALID_INPUT), never coerced to "omitted".

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE PLAN, flagged for review: case 1 with a candidateId supplied returns a
NO-CANDIDATE-RECORDED warning. The outcome is unchanged (still approves, still writes no Review —
there is nothing truthful to bind to), so DoD item 5 holds exactly for the legacy caller who
passes no candidateId. Without it, a reviewer who names bytes on a project with no candidate
records gets a silently unbound approval, which is the failure mode this card exists to close.

qaApprove.ts: `candidateId` added to inputSchema + the params cast; description now states the
hard gate. The check sits after assertWorkerOwns/assertContextFetched/summary validation — so
those refusals keep their precedence and no existing test changes meaning — and before the Review
write, the updateTask, the touchWorker and every chat side effect. First write in the handler is
still updateTask, so a refusal genuinely moves not one byte and leaves .moe/reviews absent.
The result literal is NOT restructured: `warning` (singular) is still the commit-evidence warning
alone, `commitEvidence` is untouched, `message` is untouched. Only `warnings` changed, from
`warning ? [warning] : []` to a collected array of the commit warning and the binding warning —
which is the rail's "add to it", not a restructure.

qaReject.ts: identical argument, identical helper call placed right after assertContextFetched
(before every write), identical Review with decision 'reject' and summary = params.reason. Its
reopen/failed-item/escalation behaviour is untouched. Its result gains `warnings` only when a
binding warning exists (spread, not an always-present key), so no existing caller's shape moves.

REVIEW WRITE ORDER, and why. recordReview runs BEFORE updateTask in both tools. A DONE task with
no Review is the exact hole this card closes; a Review whose status write then failed is merely a
truthful record that the decision was made. The write is awaited and never wrapped in try/catch,
so an injected writeEntity failure surfaces to the caller and nothing reaches DONE. reviewerId is
`params.workerId || 'human'` — the IDE/human approval path carries no workerId, and 'human' is the
default sender moe.chat_send already documents.

No attempt fence added to either tool, per the plan and the frozen contract: QA never holds the
attempt, and criterion 3 deliberately finalizes attempt-A-1 so the ATTEMPT_FINALIZING hold is
inert at the moment of the refusal.

Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exit 0.
`npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/tools/qaReject.test.ts src/tools/qaOwnership.test.ts
src/state/candidateStore.test.ts` exit 0 — 4 files, 80 passed, 0 failed. No pre-existing QA test
needed a change, which is the evidence for the additive-adoption rail.

Giving the review store an update path for a re-review - rejected: reviews are an append-only audit trail, so a second review is a second record and the update function must not exist at all. planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Both dependencies landed and QA-approved, so this task builds on known bytes rather than declared intent. Its list-by-task function already sorts by createdAt then id, which is precisely the current-candidate selection rule the frozen contract names - reusing it keeps one definition of current instead of two that can drift.
